tools.name: wi_webinar_delete
tools.description: Delete or replace something on the connected WordPress site — irreversible. Runs only an ability that is verified as destructive: delete a campaign, a webhook, registrants (single or all), the logs, the attendee questions, or the HC import that replaces a campaign. Writes abilities are not run here;

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "?src=registry" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: wi_webinar · Private data: wi_webinar · Public sink: wi_webinar, wi_webinar_delete · Destructive: wi_webinar, wi_webinar_delete.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: wi_webinar · Private data: wi_webinar · Public sink: wi_webinar, wi_webinar_delete · Destructive: wi_webinar, wi_webinar_delete

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "wi_webinar" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
